basics.name: Smayan A. Khanna
basics.label: Incoming PhD Student in Data Science (UCSD) | MS Computer Science (UChicago)
basics.summary: MS Computer Science student focused on AI for Science, especially representation learning and coarse-graining for physical and biological systems using geometric deep learning and graph neural networks.

work.name: University of Chicago - James Franck Institute, Vitelli Group
work.summary: Researching deep-learning techniques for representation learning in biological and physical systems; developed contrastive GNN-based methods and led a first-author project on scaling behavior of graph contrastive learning.
highlights: Researching deep-learning techniques for representation learning in biological and physical systems
Developed a contrastive algorithm using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and statistical physics techniques to optimally coarse-grain inhomogeneous graph data
Led a first-author research project analyzing the effectiveness and scaling behavior of Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) for unsupervised graph classification

work.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Dunkel Group
work.summary: Conducted research with Prof. Jörn Dunkel and the Flavell Lab on the mathematical brain-behavior link in C. elegans.
highlights: Developed a Julia pipeline which facilitated the analysis and visualization of neural trace activity datasets
Applied PCA, graph theory, and compressed sensing in Julia for dimensionality reduction of neural circuits
Identified a superior neural basis for the signal reconstruction of timeseries data using Matching Pursuit, outperforming randomly sampled bases by ~20% reconstruction accuracy

work.name: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, Ferguson Lab (University of Chicago)
work.summary: Co-developed generative backmapping models for proteins/DNA using Conditional Flow Matching and EGNNs; optimized inference and evaluated ODE solvers.
highlights: Co-developed a generative model using Conditional Flow Matching and Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) to back-map protein and DNA traces from coarse-grained simulations

Trained and fine-tuned the model on DNA-protein structures, optimizing inference time by evaluating different ODE solvers and achieving over 99% reconstruction accuracy, outperforming previous models by 3%

work.name: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, Tokmakoff Group & Prof. Andrew Ferguson (University of Chicago)
work.summary: Generated all-atom MD simulations of DNA for T-jump spectroscopy studies; automated topology creation and cluster workflows.
highlights: Streamlined nucleotide topologies, replica-exchange simulations, and cluster jobs via automation scripts

work.name: The Science Biome

highlights: Grew channel to 2K subscribers and 90K+ views
Recognized by Prof. Steven Strogatz for a differential-equations video project
Featured/interviewed by Mumbai Mirror and The Times of India
